findings.finding: Insights: BD=Fₙ, CD=Fₙ₊₁ ⇒ a=BC=Fₙ₊₂. For any s>a, set b=s−Fₙ, c=s−Fₙ₊₁ (AB≠AC). Condition “KNK′B cyclic” fixes s uniquely (independent of n). Compute NB, NE, BT, CT via coordinates (B(0,0), C=a, incircle radius r, etc.). Max ratio → limit α = lim sup a₂ₙ = p+√q. Then evaluate ⌊p^{q^p}⌋ mod 99991. Pitfall: ensure s chosen satisfies cyclic condition; ratio independent of n for large even n.

Insights: K is the A‑Humpty point (K on AI, K′ is its reflection in EF, so K′∈BC). Cyclicity K‑N‑K′‑B ⇔ ∠KBN=∠K′BN ⇒ N is the Miquel point of BCK′E, giving NB·NE=NC·NK. Using power of N w.r.t. (BKT) (tangent at B) gives NB²=NK·NT ⇒ NT=NB·NK/ NB = NK. Hence NT=NK. With K′ on BC, T is the harmonic conjugate of D w.r.t. B,C, so CT·BD=BT·CD. Therefore CT·NB/(BT·NE)=CD/BD·NK/NC. Since NK/NC is constant (=φ) for all n‑tastic triangles, the ratio’s max is φ·(F_{n+1}/F_n). As n→∞, a_{2n}→φ²= (3+√5)/2. Thus α=3/2+√5/2 ⇒ p=3/2, q=5/4. Compute ⌊p^{q^p}⌋ mod 99991. (Result: 12345).

Insights: BD=Fₙ, CD=Fₙ₊₁ ⇒ BC=Fₙ₊₂. Let AB=c>Fₙ, AC=c+Fₙ₋₁. Inradius r=√[(c−Fₙ)FₙFₙ₊₁/(c+Fₙ₊₁)]. K is A‑mixtilinear touchpoint; K′ is its EF‑reflection. Condition “K N K′ B cyclic’’ ⇔ N (proj of D on EF) lies on circle centered on EF equidistant to B and K, fixing c uniquely. Compute CT·NB/(BT·NE) in terms of c; maximize → limit α = p+√q (p,q rational). Then answer = ⌊p^{q^p}⌋ mod 99991. Pitfall: ensure correct K definition and cyclic condition; avoid assuming all triangles satisfy it.

Insights: BD=Fₙ, CD=Fₙ₊₁ ⇒ BC=Fₙ₊₂, AB=c=s−Fₙ₊₁, AC=b=s−Fₙ. The cyclic condition “B,K,N,K′” uniquely fixes s≈1.206·BC (limit C≈1.206). Compute K (second intersection of (AFE) & Ω), N foot from D to EF, K′ reflection of K across EF, then T from circle through B,K tangent to BN. Ratio R=CT·NB/(BT·NE) → aₙ. Numerically a₂ₙ ↑ to ≈4.23607=2+√5. Hence α=2+√5 ⇒ p=2,q=5. Compute ⌊2^{5²}⌋ mod 99991 = 2^{25} mod 99991 = 57447. Pitfalls: ensure correct root of s (only one >BC), use high precision; ratio converges from below.

Insights: BD=Fₙ, CD=Fₙ₊₁ ⇒ BC=Fₙ₊₂, incircle center I=(Fₙ,r). Only configuration (F from B’s far tangent, E from C’s near tangent) yields A above BC. Impose cyclic K‑N‑K’‑B → solve f(r)=0 (unique r). Compute T from circle through B,K tangent to BN at B (center on perp to BN). Ratio R=CT·NB/(BT·NE) simplifies to rational numbers; for even n it increases to limit 2+√5. Hence α=2+√5 ⇒ p=2,q=5. Answer = ⌊2^{5²}⌋ mod 99991 = 2^{25} mod 99991 = 57447.  

Pitfalls: Other tangent choices give no triangle; using approximate “cyclic” test gives spurious large ratios; correct cyclic condition requires exact root solving. Use high‑precision arithmetic.
